warnings.why: While Armenia has made progress, reporting 100% urban access to basic sanitation is inconsistent with international development reports which typically place the figure significantly lower due to infrastructure gaps in secondary cities and peri-urban areas.
The reported 32.6% is significantly lower than recent JMP (Joint Monitoring Programme) estimates for urban sanitation in Uganda, which generally indicate higher levels of access to basic services.
The figure of 21.8% is extremely low even for the DRC's urban context, suggesting a potential data collection error or a misclassification of what constitutes 'basic' sanitation in the survey used.

policy: model memory is advisory; unsupported suspicions cannot overrule official data
